Article Title: MS Dhoni at CSK: 5 titles, 10 finals and a new role ahead of IPL 2027
Article Text:
MS Dhoni

By the numbers: Dhoni's CSK legacy

Achievement Record IPL titles as captain 5 IPL finals 10 Playoff appearances 12 editions CSK IPL matches as captain 221 Overall CSK T20 appearances as captain 244 Matches won 145 Matches lost 96 Tied matches 1 No results 2 Winning percentage 59.42% Champions League T20 trophies 2

Five titles and a place among IPL's greatest captains

Ten finals highlight Chennai's consistency under Dhoni

His overall IPL captaincy numbers

NEW DELHI: Chennai Super Kings ' legendary association with MS Dhoni is entering a new phase. Ahead of IPL 2027, the former captain is set to take up the position of Team Mentor, marking a transition from leading the team on the field to guiding its next generation from the dugout.Since CSK's debut in the inaugural IPL season in 2008, Dhoni has played a central role in shaping the franchise's identity.His leadership brought Chennai five IPL championships and two Champions League T20 titles, while establishing the team as one of the most consistent sides in the competition.Championship years: 2010, 2011, 2018, 2021 and 2023.Champions League T20 victories: 2010 and 2014.Dhoni's record of five IPL trophies puts him alongside former Mumbai Indians skipper Rohit Sharma for the most championships won by a captain.His achievement in 2010 and 2011 was particularly significant, as he became the first captain to win back-to-back IPL titles.These championship victories helped establish Chennai as a major force in the league and cemented Dhoni's reputation as one of the competition's most successful leaders.CSK's remarkable playoff record stands out as one of the biggest achievements of the Dhoni era. The franchise qualified for the playoffs in 12 editions and reached the final on 10 occasions.Maintaining such a high level of performance over multiple seasons demonstrated the consistency of Dhoni's leadership and the strength of the team he helped build.Dhoni's leadership record extends beyond Chennai Super Kings.Including his 14 matches as captain of Rising Pune Supergiant in 2016, he led teams in 235 IPL matches, securing 136 victories at a win rate of 58.37%.For CSK, his overall T20 captaincy record stands at 244 matches, including Champions League T20 fixtures, with 145 wins, 96 defeats, one tie and two matches ending without a result.Dhoni captained Chennai from 2008 through 2025, with the exception of a brief period in 2022 when Ravindra Jadeja took over the responsibility. He later passed the full-time captaincy to Ruturaj Gaikwad.His appointment as Team Mentor ahead of IPL 2027 represents a new responsibility within the CSK setup. Although his role has evolved, Dhoni's experience and understanding of the game will continue to be an important part of the franchise's plans.
Article Summary: MS Dhoni is set to take up the position of Team Mentor ahead of IPL 2027. Dhoni captained Chennai from 2008 through 2025, with the exception of a brief period in 2022 when Ravindra Jadeja took over the responsibility. His overall T20 captaincy record stands at 244 matches, with 145 wins, 96 defeats, one tie and two matches ending without a result.

Article Title: Daman U-turn fails to lift cloud over Kalyan Chaubey’s AIFF future
Article Text:
All India Football Federation (AIFF) president Kalyan Chaubey

Panaji:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The newly-elected committee of the Daman and Diu Football Association has offered All India Football Federation (AIFF) president Kalyan Chaubey a lifeline by submitting a new list of delegates for next month’s all-important general body meeting and elections.Outgoing Daman FA president Amit Khemani had named general secretary Walter Pereira and technical director Altamash Shaikh as the two delegates. The list was emailed to AIFF electoral officer Rajeev Sharma before the deadline of Nov 13.However, after Pereira, a former Mumbai-based referee and match commissioner, was elected unopposed as president on Saturday, Daman sent a new list to AIFF.“The new list, sent after the deadline, has the names of Pereira and Kalyan Chaubey,” a senior official told TOI. “The electoral officer has not taken a decision on the delegates from Daman since elections were pending until the cut-off date. A decision is likely to be taken later, in accordance with the AIFF constitution.”According to sources, elections in Daman have also come under scrutiny for not adhering to the National Sports Governance Act, 2025, largely due to absence of a mandatory Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) list and the size of its executive committee.Newly-elected president Pereira did not respond to calls and messages.Sharma, on Sunday, cleared the delegate list from 29 states while the fate of states where elections are held beyond the deadline, like Daman, Pondicherry FA, Uttarakhand State FA, Jammu & Kashmir FA, and Indian Football Association (West Bengal), hangs in the balance.According to the official delegate list, former AIFF president Praful Patel will represent WIFA at the general body and is eligible to contest elections.According to Sharma, “any intimation received after this deadline (of Sept 13), and any change in the names after it, shall be permitted only with the approval of the electoral officer, in accordance with Article 4.2 of Schedule III of the Constitution.”
Article Summary: The Daman and Diu Football Association has offered All India Football Federation (AIFF) president Kalyan Chaubey a lifeline by submitting a new list of delegates. Outgoing Daman FA president Amit Khemani had named general secretary Walter Pereira and technical director Altamash Shaikh as the two delegates. The list was emailed to AIFF electoral officer Rajeev Sharma before the deadline of Nov 13.

Article Title: 'Abusive language': Yashveer Goud reveals why India celebrated fiercely after U19 Asia Cup final win over Pakistan
Article Text:
Image credit: BCCI

'Return bhi dena padta hai'

India bounce back to beat Pakistan in dramatic final

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Which player do you think was crucial to India's success in the final? Mohit Ulva Lakshya Raichandani Aaryavir Sehwag Manal Chauhan 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

India's celebrations after winning the U19 Asia Cup final against Pakistan were full of emotion. Now, young batter Yashveer Goud has revealed what led to the players' reactions after the memorable victory. Goud claimed that there was an exchange of words, including abusive language, when India lost to Pakistan in the group stage on Diwali."We had lost the match on Diwali. There was some exchange of words between us, including abusive language. We couldn't say anything after losing that match. We were waiting for the final. We wanted to perform well and show what India is capable of," Goud told Sports Today.Goud also explained why the Indian players celebrated the way they did after winning the final. According to him, they wanted to respond in the same manner as their Pakistani opponents had reacted after the group-stage match."We were doing the same thing they had done. They were silent and we were silent too. We were wearing the proud Indian jersey. We were waiting for this moment. Return bhi dena padta hai. Everyone was emotional," he added.India had lost to Pakistan by three wickets in the group stage despite scoring 208.The defeat came on Diwali, making the loss even more disappointing for the young Indian team.India had posted 208 in the group-stage match, with Arjun Rajput scoring an unbeaten 107 off just 85 balls. However, Hamza Zahoor's unbeaten 100 helped Pakistan recover from 61/5 and complete a three-wicket victory.India bounced back strongly in the semi-finals, beating Afghanistan by eight wickets. Captain Lakshya Raichandani led the way with 93 runs to set up another meeting with Pakistan in the final.Pakistan produced a strong batting performance in the title clash, scoring 337/9. Usman Khan led the charge with 107, while Abdul Qadir scored 80 and captain Farhan Yousaf contributed 63.India started their chase well, with Raichandani scoring 80 and Aaryavir Sehwag making 58. However, Pakistan fought back and left India struggling at 252/8.Manal Chauhan kept India's hopes alive with 47 off 32 balls. But his dismissal at 309/9 left Mohit Ulva with just one wicket remaining.Ulva kept his calm and found support from Chigurupati Venkata. The pair added 30 runs for the last wicket to take India across the finish line. Ulva remained unbeaten on 49 off just 26 balls as India reached 339/9 to register a thrilling one-wicket victory on the final ball.The win helped India dethrone Pakistan as U19 Asia Cup champions and completed a memorable comeback after their group-stage defeat.
Article Summary: India beat Pakistan by one wicket in the U19 Asia Cup final. Young batter Yashveer Goud has revealed what led to the players' reactions after the memorable victory. Goud claimed that there was an exchange of words, including abusive language, when India lost to Pakistan in the group stage on Diwali.

Article Title: 'Iceman': Sunil Gavaskar compares Mohit Ulva to MS Dhoni after U19 Asia Cup final heroics
Article Text:
Sunil Gavaskar and MS Dhoni

Gavaskar Compares Ulva To MS Dhoni

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Gavaskar Recalls Dhoni's 2011 World Cup Moment

Legendary Indian cricketer Sunil Gavaskar has praised young batter Mohit Ulva for his match-winning performance against Pakistan in the U19 Asia Cup 2026 final. Gavaskar compared Ulva's calmness under pressure to former India captain MS Dhoni after the youngster helped India pull off an incredible victory.India were chasing a target of 338 but looked almost certain to lose after slipping to 252/8.However, lower-order batters Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva turned the match around by scoring the runs needed in the final eight overs.Coming in at No. 10, Ulva played a stunning unbeaten knock of 49 runs from just 26 balls. His innings included five fours and three sixes. With three runs needed off the final delivery, he stepped out and hit a boundary over extra cover to seal India's victory.Gavaskar was impressed by the youngster's ability to stay calm in such a tense situation and compared his finishing skills to Dhoni."He (Ulva) showed coolness like MS Dhoni. Iceman. He just came out, hit a four, and saw. The non-striker was very happy. He took his helmet off, kept it down, and then raised his hands," Gavaskar said on Sony Sports.Gavaskar also compared Ulva's winning shot and celebration to Dhoni's famous six that sealed India's victory in the 2011 ODI World Cup final."Had MS Dhoni been there, he would have done like that too. You have seen the way MS Dhoni raised his bat after hitting the six in the World Cup. It's memorable, and this is also memorable," Gavaskar added.He also praised the Indian youngsters for refusing to give up despite losing eight wickets while chasing a big target."The biggest thing was that they never gave up. The score was 252 when the eighth wicket fell. More than 80 runs were required for a win. However, they kept their target in front of them," he added.
Article Summary: Mohit Ulva played a stunning unbeaten knock of 49 runs from just 26 balls. His innings included five fours and three sixes. With three runs needed off the final delivery, he stepped out and hit a boundary. Gavaskar was impressed by the youngster's ability to stay calm in such a tense situation.

Article Title: Complaint alleges irregularities in GFI camp funds, treasurer rejects charges
Article Text:
Gymnastics Federation of India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: A complaint submitted to the Sports Authority of India (SAI) on Sunday has accused the Gymnastics Federation of India (GFI) of possible diversion and misappropriation of govt funds released for national coaching camps in Bhubaneswar, alleging that athletes, coaches and vendors are yet to receive payments despite the federation submitting a utilisation certificate (UC) for the expenditure.In a representation to SAI, a copy of which is with TOI, former international gymnast and GFI general body member Rakesh Kumar Patra alleged that a little more than Rs 14.42 lakh sanctioned for men’s and women’s artistic gymnastics camps held ahead of the Asian Championships was shown as utilised, even though several liabilities remain unsettled.The complaint by the national coach claims that hospitality provider Swastik Hospitality is owed nearly Rs 12 lakh, while physiotherapist Yash Jaiswal and several gymnasts and coaches, including Dipa Karmakar, are awaiting reimbursements.Seeking an independent financial and vigilance inquiry, Patra has also sought scrutiny of GFI president Sudhir Mital, treasurer Kaushik Bidiwala and the chartered accountant firm Narender Singh & Co., which certified the utilisation certificate.Responding to the allegations, Bidiwala denied any irregularity in the issuance of the utilisation certificate. “A utilisation certificate cannot be issued without proper documentation and supporting records.If the documents are not available, even the chartered accountant will not certify it,” Bidwala told TOI.He said allegations and certification of expenditure were separate matters and maintained that the UC process involved verification of original documents and proofs.On the issue of pending reimbursements, Bidiwala said delays, if any, could be linked to procedural requirements rather than withholding of payments. “If any reimbursements are pending, it is not because there is an intention to withhold anyone’s money. There may be processing delays, but the money will not be stopped and beneficiaries will receive their payments,” he said.The treasurer added that he was focused on the welfare of the sport and cautioned that prolonged disputes could hurt gymnastics’ image and discourage parents from encouraging children to take up the discipline.
Article Summary: Gymnastics Federation of India (GFI) accused of possible diversion and misappropriation of govt funds released for national coaching camps in Bhubaneswar. Former international gymnast and GFI general body member Rakesh Kumar Patra alleged that a little more than Rs 14.42 lakh was shown as utilised.

Article Title: Teenager Mirra Andreeva joins elite group of tennis stars after winning WTA Finals without losing a single set
Article Text:
Mirra Andreeva (AP Photo)

Andreeva joins elite group of tennis stars

Svitolina praises Andreeva after final

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Russian tennis star Mirra Andreeva capped off a remarkable season by winning the WTA Finals without losing a single set. The 19-year-old defeated Ukraine's Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in Sunday's final to finish the tournament with five wins from five matches.The victory also helped Andreeva reach a career-best world ranking of No. 2, behind Kazakhstan's Elena Rybakina.Along with the title, Andreeva earned $3.37 million in prize money and a unique ultraviolet purple Mercedes-Benz convertible. However, there is one thing she still needs before she can drive her new car: a driver's license.“This is an amazing motivation for me to get my driver's license as fast as I can,” she said. “If not, then look, I have five people on my team. I'm going to be a passenger's princess forever, that's also an option for me.”With this victory, Andreeva became only the 11th player to win the WTA Finals without dropping a set. She joined legendary names such as Chris Evert, Martina Navratilova and Serena Williams.Speaking after her win, the teenager expressed her happiness at joining such an elite group.“I'm super privileged to put my name in that group,” she said.Andreeva also took a moment to appreciate her own hard work during the awards ceremony. Wearing a jacket with the words 'I want to thank myself', she spoke about the effort and dedication behind her success.“I want to thank myself for always doing the hard work, for never quitting, for always believing in myself, for not taking the days off, for working every day and for committing to what I have to do,” she said. “Just thanks to myself without any reason.”The final was closely fought, with both players exchanging breaks and battling hard from the baseline. However, Andreeva won five of the last six games to seal the title in just under two hours.The match ended after Svitolina missed an easy smash, giving Andreeva the victory. The players did not shake hands after the match, continuing the practice followed by Ukrainian players against Russian and Belarusian opponents since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022.Despite the situation, Andreeva congratulated Svitolina on her season and praised her comeback as a mother.“You're an amazing mom to come back and do this. It's super hard,” she said. “I just wish you the best of luck for the next season.”Svitolina also acknowledged Andreeva's performance, saying, “I put everything out there and she played incredible.”
Article Summary: Russian tennis star Mirra Andreeva won the WTA Finals without losing a set. The 19-year-old defeated Ukraine's Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in Sunday's final. She earned $3.37 million in prize money and a unique ultraviolet purple Mercedes- Benz convertible.

Article Title: Indian lawn bowlers ready for New Zealand challenge after landmark year
Article Text:
(From left) Sunil Bahadur, Reshma Kumari, Pinki Singh and Dinesh Kumar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: It has been a good year for Indian lawn bowls. Putul Sonowal won bronze at the Champion of Champions tournament, India claimed four gold medals at the Asian Championships, and recently added a bronze in the mixed pairs event at the Malaysian Open.Perhaps more significantly, the Bowling Federation of India (BFI) received recognition from the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports as the governing body for lawn bowls in the country. It was a major boost for the sport as it looks to build towards the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.Before that, however, the focus is on the Test series against New Zealand, scheduled for Nov 16, 17 and 18 in Auckland as part of the centenary celebrations of sporting ties between the two nations.Each Test will comprise five matches: men’s pairs, women’s pairs, mixed fours, mixed pairs 1 and mixed pairs 2. India will be represented by Dinesh Kumar, Sunil Bahadur and rising player Reshma Kumari, all from Jharkhand, alongside Arjuna Awardee and Commonwealth Games gold medallist Pinki Singh.Speaking about the opportunity, Dinesh, a five-time CWG participant, said: “Getting the opportunity to represent India in the Test series is a great moment for us.We are going there with the aim of delivering a strong performance.”Having trained together since 2008, Dinesh and Sunil have enjoyed a remarkable journey. The Ranchi-based duo now hopes to make the most of international competition as Indian lawn bowls continues to gain momentum on the global stage.“We are travelling regularly and gaining experience against some of the world’s best players. Every match becomes a learning opportunity. Even when we lose, we understand where we need to improve. Competing against experienced international players accelerates our development,” said Sunil, who partnered Reshma to win bronze in the mixed pairs event at the Malaysian Open earlier this month.The medal was a particularly significant achievement for Reshma, who was previously a 1500m runner but switched sports in 2023 after struggling with injuries. She is now eager to make the most of her upcoming tour to New Zealand.“Things are progressing well, my game is improving, and I am determined to take full advantage of every opportunity that comes my way,” said the youngster.While the players are pleased with the progress the sport has made in recent years, they believe India would benefit from hosting more invitational tournaments, similar to those regularly staged in established lawn bowls nations.BFI president Ravi Bengani shares that ambition. Having previously expressed confidence that India can challenge for as many as four gold medals at the 2030 Commonwealth Games, he is focused on creating more opportunities for players to gain exposure at the highest level.“Besides participating in international tournaments, we have signed an agreement with Bowls New Zealand. We will bring their coaches and technical officials to India and provide our players with greater exposure and expertise,” Bengani had said.For now, however, the immediate challenge lies in Auckland, where India’s lawn bowlers will look to cap a landmark year by making a statement against New Zealand.
Article Summary: India's lawn bowlers will take on New Zealand in a Test series in Auckland. Dinesh Kumar, Sunil Bahadur, Reshma Kumari and Pinki Singh will represent India. The Test series is part of the centenary celebrations of sporting ties between the two nations.

Article Title: Three LA 2028 quotas at first attempt! India make best start to Olympic shooting cycle in decades
Article Text:
Jaypal Malviya

Three LA 2028 quotas at first attempt

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Indian shooters dominate ISSF People's Choice Awards race

NEW DELHI: India have made their strongest start to an Olympic qualification cycle in shooting in at least 16 years, securing three quota places for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics at the ISSF World Championship Rifle/Pistol/Shotgun in Doha, Qatar.For the first time across five consecutive Olympic cycles, stretching from London 2012 to LA28, Indian shooters have secured three Olympic quotas at the very first qualification event. The landmark achievement, made possible by podium finishes across all three shooting disciplines — rifle, pistol and shotgun — has given India an early advantage in the race for Olympic berths.Jaypal Malviya opened India's account with a silver medal in the men's 10m air pistol event. Niraj Kumar followed with bronze in the men's 50m rifle 3 positions, before Vivaan Kapoor completed the impressive haul with silver in the men's trap.The three podium finishes not only secured India's first Olympic quotas for LA28 but also underlined the growing depth across the country's shooting programme.India's Doha performance represents a significant improvement on its opening-event returns in the previous four Olympic qualification cycles.The country secured two quotas at the 2010 Munich World Championships ahead of London 2012, followed by just one at the 2014 Granada World Championships before the Rio 2016 Games.The tally improved to two at the 2018 Changwon World Championships ahead of Tokyo 2020, while India collected two quotas from the 2022 Osijek Shotgun World Championships and Cairo Rifle/Pistol World Championships before Paris 2024.The three quotas in Doha in 2026 have therefore set a new benchmark for India's opening performance in an Olympic qualification campaign since the London 2012 cycle.Welcoming the achievement, National Rifle Association of India (NRAI) president Kalikesh Narayan Singh Deo said: "Starting an Olympic cycle with three quotas right at the first World Championship is a huge boost for everyone involved. What makes me happiest is that all three disciplines—rifle, pistol and shotgun—delivered podium finishes. Usually, it takes a few World Cups for the momentum to build, so getting three spots on the board this early takes a lot of pressure off the team and gives our coaching staff a clear runway to plan for Los Angeles. "NRAI secretary general Pawankumar Singh also praised the shooters for delivering under pressure against a strong international field."Winning a quota at a World Championship is never easy because every top shooter in the world is competing in the same field. Jaypal, Niraj and Vivaan kept their composure in very tight finals and earned those spots the hard way. Our high-performance team and coaches put in months of quiet work behind the scenes to get us here, and we will keep building on this start over the next two years," he said.India also finished second in the overall medal standings in Doha with 13 medals, comprising two gold, seven silver and four bronze, further underlining the strength of its campaign.India's impressive showing in international shooting has extended beyond the competition arena, with the country's shooters emerging as frontrunners in the ISSF 2026 Athlete of the Year People's Choice Awards.Four Indian shooters — Esha Singh, Elavenil Valarivan, Tilottama Sen and Sakshi Padekar — feature among the five nominees in the women's category, while Tushar Mane is leading the men's voting.Voting, which began on November 9, will close on November 18, with the winners in the men's and women's categories to be announced thereafter.
Article Summary: India secure three quota places for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics at the ISSF World Championship Rifle/Pistol/Shotgun in Doha, Qatar. The landmark achievement was made possible by podium finishes across all three shooting disciplines — rifle, pistol and shotgun. Jaypal Malviya opened India's account with a silver medal in the men's 10m air pistol event.

Article Title: ‘Sacrifice runs for Virat Kohli’: Sunil Gavaskar's big take on pressure facing Shubman Gill and Shreyas Iyer
Article Text:
India's Virat Kohli

Mid-day

Poll Vote & Share your view Was Kohli's performance in the first ODI against New Zealand commendable? Yes, he played brilliantly. He could have done better. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Legendary India batter Sunil Gavaskar has weighed in on the debate surrounding Virat Kohli 's pursuit of 100 international centuries, suggesting that a teammate making a personal sacrifice to help the star reach the landmark would bring joy to Indian cricket fans as well.Kohli was in superb touch during the first ODI against New Zealand, smashing 74 off just 51 deliveries to guide India towards victory in a low-scoring contest. However, Gavaskar raised an interesting possibility in his latest column for: had Kohli stayed at the crease for longer, captain Shubman Gill and vice-captain Shreyas Iyer could have found themselves in a difficult position.With India closing in on the target, the two batters might have had to choose between finishing the match quickly and giving Kohli an opportunity to reach his century. The prospect becomes even more significant given that Kohli is chasing the historic mark of 100 international hundreds.Gavaskar acknowledged that winning a match must remain the team's primary objective, but argued that helping a player achieve such a landmark, provided it does not compromise the result, could be a moment of collective celebration."Indians have always been fond of records and so there's always a debate about the rights and wrongs of going for it.One thing for sure that 99% of those who say they don't play for records are actually incapable talent and temperament wise of setting any and so it's easy for them to say so," Gavaskar wrote."There is not a single Indian cricket fan who does not want Kohli to get to 100 international centuries. We are all cheering for him to get there and so, if there's an occasion where some other teammate sacrifices his runs to allow him the chance to get there, the glory will not be just Kohli's but for all Indian cricket fans too," he added.Kohli eventually fell for 74 with India at 124/3 in the rain-affected contest, leaving the team with relatively little work to do in the chase. His dismissal also meant Gill and Iyer did not have to confront the possibility of managing the chase around his personal milestone.Gavaskar felt the two players were spared a potentially awkward situation, including the prospect of facing criticism from fans on social media if India had delayed sealing the victory to give Kohli a chance to complete his hundred."Kohli got out in the 70s. Gill and Iyer were thus spared any blowback if the winning runs had been hit with Kohli unbeaten in the 90s. Yes, it's a team game, but it's also good for the team if one of its members, especially a star player, gets to a personal milestone without affecting the team's chances of winning," Gavaskar pointed out.Kohli, who now plays only ODIs, has 86 international centuries to his name. He is chasing a landmark that remains exclusive to Sachin Tendulkar, the only batter to have scored 100 international hundreds.
Article Summary: Virat Kohli is chasing the historic mark of 100 international hundreds. Sunil Gavaskar says a teammate making a personal sacrifice to help the star reach the landmark would bring joy to Indian cricket fans as well. Kohli was in superb touch during the first ODI against New Zealand, smashing 74.

For more than a decade, Ronaldinho ’s playing career belonged to the past, even if his reputation as one of football’s most gifted entertainers never quite faded. When third-tier Italian club Ravenna announced his arrival in June, the prospect of seeing the Brazilian back in competitive action seemed more like an elaborate publicity exercise than a serious sporting proposition. On Sunday, at 46, he walked out in a No. 10 shirt and made it real.Ronaldinho started Ravenna’s Serie C derby against Forlì on November 15, playing the first 45 minutes of a 2-0 victory at the Stadio Bruno Benelli. It was his first appearance in a competitive professional match since leaving Fluminense in 2015, bringing an 11-year absence from the game to an end.The occasion was considerably larger than an ordinary third-tier fixture. Ravenna’s usual 5,000-capacity ground had been expanded with a temporary stand accommodating another 1,800 spectators, named “R10” in honour of the Brazilian. Flares and smoke bombs filled the stands as Andrea Bocelli’splayed over the stadium speakers, while Ronaldinho entered to a reception befitting a player whose influence on football extended far beyond the clubs he represented.Wearing Ravenna’s No. 10, the 2005 Ballon d’Or winner showed flashes of the close control and technical quality that defined his career. He did not score, nor did he create a clear opportunity for himself, but he was involved in the move that produced the opening goal.Giulio Donati put Ravenna ahead in the 36th minute with a strike from outside the penalty area, after Ronaldinho had helped set the attacking sequence in motion.He finished his half with 28 touches and an 81 per cent passing accuracy before acknowledging the supporters and making way for Matteo Maggio at the interval. Simone Rabbi added Ravenna’s second goal after the break to complete the 2-0 win.Ronaldinho had initially been expected to play around 30 minutes, but instead completed the entire first half. His contribution was necessarily limited by the circumstances of his return, yet the occasion was never solely about what he could produce over 90 minutes. Ravenna had brought one of football’s most recognisable figures back into a professional dressing room, and the response inside the Bruno Benelli showed what that meant to the club and its supporters.Speaking to Sky Italia afterwards, Ronaldinho said: “It went by too fast, that has always been football for me. Is this my last one? I don’t know. If the president keeps calling me, I will come back. It is always a pleasure. I told the president, if he needs me, then I will be here.“It was lovely to be here, playing, having the buildup in the dressing room. Football has always been the most wonderful thing in my life.”Ravenna’s announcement in June was initially met with considerable scepticism. Ronaldinho had not played professional football since his departure from Fluminense in 2015 and formally announced his retirement in 2018, aged 37. The idea that he would resume his playing career more than a decade after his last competitive appearance, particularly with a club in Italy’s third division, was difficult for many to take seriously.The move was driven by Ravenna president Ignazio Cipriani, who had bought his hometown club in June 2024. His stated ambition was to “make young people of Ravenna fall in love with football”, and signing a player he had grown up idolising offered an unusually direct way of pursuing it.Cipriani had made no secret of the fact that he wanted Ronaldinho to appear in the derby against Forlì. The Brazilian’s debut in that fixture had been the president’s dream from the beginning, and the match provided the occasion around which the club could build its return.The two men had developed a genuine friendship after being introduced by Lorenzo Tonetti, the former co-owner of Milan’s well-known Giannino restaurant, which Ronaldinho frequented during his time at AC Milan between July 2008 and January 2011. That relationship helped turn what might otherwise have remained an unlikely proposal into an agreement.Cipriani explained his admiration for the Brazilian in an interview with, saying: “I don't think there’s any other player who inspires such a love for the game as Ronaldinho does.”He also described the player's response when the possibility of returning to the pitch was raised. “That’s just how things go with Ronnie,” Cipriani told. “If there's a chance to have fun and excite people, he's all in.”Ronaldinho agreed immediately, according to Cipriani, and the arrangement extended beyond a one-off appearance. The former Barcelona and Brazil star also became a shareholder in Ravenna, giving him a stake in the club he had joined as a player. His arrival was facilitated by Cipriani, with the president's personal connection to the Brazilian central to bringing the deal together.Ronaldinho arrived in Ravenna on Friday and trained with the squad for the first time on Saturday, before being named in the starting line-up for the derby the following day. The short preparation period did little to diminish the anticipation surrounding his appearance.Ronaldinho’s return to Italy carried an additional connection to the country where he had already enjoyed one of the most memorable periods of his career. He represented AC Milan from July 2008 until January 2011, scoring his first goal in Italian football in a derby against Inter on September 28, 2008.That match was another occasion on which the Brazilian left his mark on a local rivalry, although the circumstances of Sunday's appearance were very different. At Milan, he was an established star competing at the highest level of European football. At Ravenna, he was returning at 46 to a club whose ambitions are centred on climbing the Italian divisions.Ravenna have not played in Serie B since 2008 and have never appeared in Serie A. They entered the weekend second in their Serie C regional group, with 29 points from 13 matches, while Forlì were 15th with 15 points. Ravenna had been reported to be six points behind leaders Spezia ahead of the fixture.The result preserved Ravenna’s position near the top of the table, but the larger significance of the derby was the fulfilment of a project that had seemed improbable when it was first announced. Ronaldinho's presence brought attention to a club competing outside Italy's top two divisions, while giving supporters an opportunity to see a player whose career had helped define an era of attacking football.Whether Sunday's appearance becomes a regular feature remains uncertain. Ronaldinho has not committed to a schedule of further matches, but his comments after the game left the possibility open. His willingness to return whenever Cipriani asks suggests that the derby may not necessarily be the only time he wears Ravenna's No. 10.
Article Summary: Ronaldinho returns after 11 years as Ravenna beat Forlì in local derby. Ronaldinho played the first 45 minutes of a 2-0 victory at the Stadio Bruno Benelli. Ravenna’s usual 5,000-capacity ground had been expanded with a temporary stand accommodating another 1,800 spectators.

Article Title: ‘He got greedy’: Ex-India captain's blunt take on Arshdeep Singh after four-wicket haul
Article Text:
India bowler Arshdeep Singh celebrates with teammate Virat Kohli (AP/PTI)

Jadeja impressed with Anshul Kamboj

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former India cricketer Ajay Jadeja has praised Arshdeep Singh's overall performance in India's five-wicket victory over New Zealand in the first ODI in Auckland, but believes the left-arm pacer could have avoided an expensive finish to his spell.India began their five-match ODI series with a comfortable win at Eden Park on Wednesday, November 4. In a rain-interrupted contest reduced to 32 overs per side, New Zealand were bowled out for 185 before India chased down the revised target of 143 in just 22.4 overs. Virat Kohli led the chase with a fluent 74, while Shubman Gill contributed 37 as the duo stitched together a 113-run partnership. India eventually crossed the finish line with five wickets to spare and 56 deliveries remaining.With the ball, Arshdeep was India's leading wicket-taker, claiming four wickets in his 10 overs. However, his figures of 4/70 were inflated by an expensive final over in which New Zealand tailender Blair Tickner struck him for three sixes, taking 23 runs off the over.Assessing the pacer's performance, Jadeja felt Arshdeep had been impressive for most of his spell but allowed the opportunity to complete a five-wicket haul to influence his bowling towards the end."I would call him slightly greedy. He himself said that as well. If you remove his last over, he had dismissed four batters before that and had given 40-odd runs. He got slightly greedy for the fifth wicket in the last over," Jadeja said on Sony Sports Network.Arshdeep had himself admitted after the match that the fifth wicket would have been his favourite, indicating that he was keen to complete a five-wicket haul. Despite missing out on the milestone, his four-wicket effort placed him in an exclusive group of Indian fast bowlers to achieve the feat in an ODI in New Zealand, alongside Javagal Srinath and Mohammed Shami.Jadeja, however, stressed that the expensive final over should not overshadow what Arshdeep brings to India's bowling combination. He pointed to the value of having a left-arm fast bowler in an attack that already features Jasprit Bumrah, adding that the competition for places would only benefit the team."It happens. It's natural, but Arshdeep Singh is showing that he can play in ODIs as well, which I believe is a very good thing when a left-arm seamer gets added to this attack with (Jasprit) Bumrah. The competition has increased a lot, which is very good for India," Jadeja elaborated.Jadeja also reserved praise for Anshul Kamboj, who delivered an economical spell of 2/22 from his 10 overs and walked away with the Player of the Match award.The former India batter acknowledged that Kamboj had faced questions over his bowling during his Test debut against England in 2025, particularly regarding his pace and tendency to bowl no-balls. However, he felt the youngster had shown considerable improvement in Auckland.Jadeja also suggested that Kamboj's workload before the England assignment could have contributed to his struggles, pointing out that fatigue can affect a bowler's execution. His performance against New Zealand, according to Jadeja, reflected better pace, consistency and accuracy."He bowled extremely well. The vision everyone had was that he didn't have pace when he played in England and was bowling a lot of no-balls. I think he had come after playing a lot of cricket then. So a guy also gets tired. It's not that easy. Then he was playing for the first time, but the consistency and the slight increase in his pace he showed today (Wednesday), if we talk about the accuracy amongst the four bowlers, it's Anshul Kamboj," Jadeja added.
Article Summary: India beat New Zealand by five wickets in the first ODI in Auckland. Ajay Jadeja praised Arshdeep Singh's performance, but said he could have avoided expensive final over. Jadeja also praised Anshul Kamboj's bowling, saying he had shown improvement.

Article Title: 'We wouldn't play if we weren't confident tournament could be delivered safely': ILT20 Interim COO Michael Fordham
Article Text:
Michael Fordham, ILT20's Interim COO in a file photo. (Photo by special arrangement)

Excerpts:

Q. How have things been in the past couple of months since taking over the interim COO role?

Michael Fordham:

Q. What are your biggest priorities when it comes to starting a new season? When you pitch to prospective players, to prospective teams? What is the pitch for Season 5?

Fordham:

Heading into the fifth season, the league is reasonably well established now. I think it's one of the top three T20 leagues in the world. But obviously, you don't want to rest on your laurels. ILT20 Interim COO Michael Fordham

We've been in touch with the government and the government officials every step of the way regarding their advice, and we wouldn't play this tournament if we weren't confident that it could be delivered safely. Michael Fordham, ILT20 Interim COO

Q. Many other sporting events have either been rescheduled or cancelled completely in the region. Considering the challenge that the Middle East poses at this point, how much of a difficulty has it been to convince players, coaches, staff to come into the country?

Fordham:

Andries Gous and Fakhar Zaman of Desert Vipers during Qualifier 1 of the World ILT20 between Desert Vipers and MI Emirates. (Photo Credit: ILT20)

Q. What are the contingency plans?

Fordham:

Q. What have your learnings been for the past four seasons or even the last season?

ILT20 Season 5 – Desert Vipers to begin title defence on November 21 against MI Emirates

Q. Coming to the cricket of it all. It's very important for leagues to have a good combination of local players and foreigners. And in ILT20's case, there are quite a few Associate players. So how do you ensure that everything stays in tandem?

Fordham:

File photo of Michael Fordham. (Photo by special arrangement)

Q. Do these mandatory rules restrict the teams, the coaches from picking the ideal playing XI?

Fordham:

Q. When it comes to growing a league, India and UAE are important markets. But how do you go over and above that?

Fordham:

Q. When it comes to the T20 leagues, there is significant competition among all of them for getting the best talent, the best sponsors, the broadcasters. How do you envision ILT20 standing out?

Q. What about the players in such a scenario? Some players don't play the entire season and jump to another T20 league. How can that issue be addressed?

Fordham:

Q. What is the long-term vision for the ILT20? Where do you see it going and what can be expected from the ILT20?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Fordham:

As the ILT20 prepares to enter its fifth season, interim COO Michael Fordham believes the league has established itself among the leading T20 competitions in the world. Having been involved since its inception, Fordham discusses the challenges of organising the new season amid uncertainty in the Middle East, the league's international identity, its emphasis on developing UAE and Associate cricket, and the need to build a sustainable fan base.He also explains how the ILT20 intends to differentiate itself in an increasingly crowded franchise cricket landscape, while outlining its ambitions to expand its reach and strengthen its position in the global game.It's been good. It's been busy. I've been involved in the league since since the outset, since even before Season 1, helping to put it all together and overseeing various aspects. So I familiar with the various workings of ILT20 and all of our internal teams, our stakeholders, franchises, partners, etc.So it hasn't been too much of a learning curve, but obviously it's a slightly different and expanded role. I've been in Dubai for most of that time. It's obviously been a slightly challenging time for the Middle East as a region this year. But we're hopeful that, you know, with just over a week to go, we're going to be in position to deliver a great tournament for ILT20 Season 5.Heading into the fifth season, the league is reasonably well established now. I think it's one of the top three T20 leagues in the world. So I think we've established ourselves quite well. But obviously, you don't want to rest on your laurels. You've got to continue to grow and continue to expand and continue to make everything a success.So we were keen to, first of all, get as wide a selection of players available for this season as possible. We've moved to a slightly earlier window this year. In previous years, the first three seasons, it was all played in the early part of the year, January, February time. Last year, it started in December and just finished at the beginning of January. And this year, we're at the earliest start yet, starting on the 21st of November. And I think that's a positive. I think it's probably the best window we could have chosen this year for player availability, less clash with other leagues. So a pretty clear window for that.And we've had quite a big refresh in terms of the squad compositions this year. There were not too many retentions or direct signings that each team was allowed to make after Season 4. So we had a big player auction on the 1st of October. So during the summer, we had a player registration open for that. And the auction was held on the 1st of October, which went very well. All the squads were chosen there. I would say they're pretty well-balanced teams. It's pretty hard to tell which team looks the strongest, which is always a good sign. And we've got a lot of good new players into the league. So I think we've achieved that aim of bringing in some different players.And this is always an attractive league for players to come to. Players like coming to the UAE. They're familiar with it. They love the facilities, the weather, the hotels. They don't have to travel too much during the season, which is a positive compared to a lot of other leagues. I think we've achieved the objective of getting a good group of players in for this year.Now it's two things, really. One is deliver a smooth season operationally. Make sure that everything goes well in the venues and all of the logistics and everything like that. And the other is obviously try and make it as big a commercial and financial success as possible for the league and all of its stakeholders, including the franchises.To be honest, it hasn't been too much of a challenge convincing players and other partners to come to the UAE. I think players are pretty confident that we will put the right measures in place to ensure their safety. We've been in touch with the government and the government officials every step of the way regarding their advice, and we wouldn't play this tournament if we weren't confident that it could be delivered safely.It's been a tough year for the Middle East as a region, starting from February onwards. But actually in the UAE for the last few months, it's been pretty quiet on that front. And every indication is that we'll be able to launch safely and smoothly.That said, it would be remiss if we didn't have some kind of contingency plans in place. So we have looked at alternate solutions if the situation did escalate. But I think at the moment, everybody is confident that the season can go ahead smoothly.As I'm sure you're aware, the Abu Dhabi T10 is currently taking place just down the road at Abu Dhabi. That has started off very well without incident. So actually, that means quite a few of the players from the ILT20 are already in the UAE. The Abu Dhabi Golf Championships took place last weekend with most of the top golfers from around Europe and around the world taking part. There's another big golf tournament in Dubai this weekend. Those tournaments are going ahead. So actually, I think the outlook for sports in the UAE hopefully is pretty positive right now.We have explored other possible venues. There is one in particular that would be considered in the case of things escalating. But as we currently stand, we are 100% full steam ahead for UAE and starting here at Dubai International Stadium next Saturday.Fordham: I think the first thing you've got to think about with any sports property, not just cricket, is actually making sure that the sport itself, the action on the field is as good as possible and as competitive as possible. And over the four seasons, I think we've done that well. The fact that we've had four different winners of this tournament in four seasons is pretty exciting and shows that it's a pretty level playing field in the teams in terms of their ability.The on-field product of this event is very strong, not just the players but the match officials, everything like that. We have really good six franchises, some of whom have teams in other leagues, some of whom don't, but they're committed to making this season a success. So cricket-wise, I think we're in great shape, and we'll be the same again this year.Beyond that, we've got to try and make it as big a tournament as possible with its marketing, with its social media presence, with its broadcast presence. We have a fantastic TV partner in India with Zee, who are fully committed to this and showcasing this league through all of their channels. They have a new channel this year (United8 Sports) so that's a bit exciting to see how that goes.And then in terms of our marketing activities as a league, it's a couple of things. We want to make it as big as possible for those who are viewing it around the world, both on broadcast and on digital. So we've invested a lot this year with social media and other content providers in that regard. We've got some new partners coming on board. And then with our promotions in the UAE, obviously that's all about trying to get as many people in the stadium as possible, selling as many tickets as possible, and creating as much buzz as we can in the UAE. And with that in mind, we're trying a few new things this year to try and increase the awareness and increase the buzz throughout the tournament.It's quite an interesting squad composition with this league. It's quite a mix of players and one of the things we're very proud about, one of the things I'm very passionate about, is ILT20's role in developing cricket in certain markets and spreading the game globally.First and foremost, that includes the UAE. So in each team, there has to be a minimum of four UAE players in the squad, two of whom have to play at least in the matchday playing eleven. We've seen some fantastic performances from UAE players over the four seasons so far, and I'm sure that will be the same again. The UAE players were very much in demand at the auction.In addition to that, there has to be an Associate player from another nation within the playing eleven. And we've got players all over the cricketing world really being signed up in those associate squads. So USA, Scotland, Namibia, Nepal, all sorts of different places. And that's fantastic to give players from other countries an opportunity.And in addition to that, we're very committed to growing cricket and having our players in the other Gulf countries. So we're very happy to have partnerships with both Kuwait cricket and Saudi Arabian cricket. So there's just a player from each of those nations in every squad. And actually, this year, we're also going to be having some match officials, umpires from those two countries with the match officials team.We're very proud of our role in growing cricket in the region. This year also, we have a high number of Afghanistan players with a partnership with the Afghan board. There's an Irish player in every squad. So it really is a very multicultural, multinational tournament with the players and probably one of the most, probably the most international T20 tournament. And I think that's something that's pretty exciting and unique about this league.Not really. We've got two UAE players and another associate in the match XI. So there's another eight players that can come from any of the Full Member or other Associate countries. So that's a pretty wide selection of talent available. And I think you've seen that with the players signed up for the auction.You've got pretty much every Test nation and many Associate nations represented in our squads. It's a real mix of experienced T20 superstars and some younger upcoming players. We've got people like Thomas Rew, who's playing for the first time this year. He was one of the top young players from England. Him playing alongside, and against legends of the game who've been around for a long time, like a Faf du Plessis or Andre Russell's. It's something that makes this a really compelling tournament. So I think that the franchises sort of lean into that and enjoy the strategy around building a team from different nationalities and different skill sets. So yeah, there are not too many issues there. I think it's something that people like about this league.You're right that those probably are the two key markets. India, clearly, due to its massive passion for cricket and size of the commercial market and geographic and time zone proximity to the UAE, is obviously vital.The UAE is our home market. Clearly any sports competition needs to have its local fan base. So it is key that we promote and produce coverage into the UAE and the wider Middle East. That's vital.But as I said, this is an incredibly international tournament with players from all over the world. So we have to have broadcast coverage and digital coverage in every cricketing nation, from Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, UK, Australia, South Africa, the Caribbean, the USA. These are all key markets for us. And all of our partners play a role in that. Broadcasters, other media partners, and our sponsors all play a role in promoting into those places.Fordham: A few things really. As you say, it is a crowded schedule for T20 leagues. Every country in the cricket world pretty much has a T20 league now or a T10 league So I think we stand out with quite a few things.One is the franchises. We have a real great mix of franchises. Three who have brand IPL and three who don't. That's quite a mix rather than being a league that is all IPL teams like maybe the SA20.The international nature of this tournament from its playing base, probably more players from more different nationalities than any other tournament makes this one stand out and feel quite compelling.The UAE as a destination itself is a huge multicultural hotspot and a melting pot of people from all over the world. And I think that's reflected in the event. But yeah, this being a place that people love to come, whether that's fans and tourists on holiday because of the weather at this time of year, players love coming here.So I think we've sort of created quite a kind of niche for ourselves and a very appealing tournament for players to come in. They get well looked after. They enjoy bringing their families out to Dubai. It's a great place to be at any time of year, especially this time of year when the cricket is on. So hopefully some of those are the factors that mean that we can stand out in a crowded market.Yeah, it's a good question. And you hit on one of the central challenges of global cricket, not just faced by this league. But as I said right at the start of this, the most important thing about any sports competition is the on-field product.By that, I mean the competitiveness and crucially, players trying their hardest and bona fide competition between the players, between the teams. And I really feel like we have that in this tournament.I remember talking to some of the umpires last season, and they said that they felt this was as competitive tournament as any in the world. And I definitely feel that.The players seem to care for the teams that they play for. A team like the Desert Vipers or a Gulf Giants who aren't in other leagues in the world, they've built that sort of culture of wanting to play for the team and, built that team identity and team culture through the owners and the management.It definitely feels that this isn't just a case of them (players) turning up at another tournament and not really caring what happens. This is a bona fide competitive league where the on-field actions take precedence.The long-term vision is simply to carry on what we're doing, but continue to grow each year and do new things. You know, grow our audience, grow our viewership, grow our attendances in stadium, grow commercial revenues, become even more established as one of the top T20 leagues in the world. I think we can grow more across the Middle East.Our partnerships with Kuwait and Saudi Arabia are really exciting. I think this is a real region which has got a lot of potential for cricket. Actually, a lot of talent on the field coming through, but actually a lot of fans that we can engage better with and do more with. So it's just more of the same, really.Growing, providing entertainment for everybody, and, you know, being a well-run, well-respected league. Continuing in that regard would be the long-term objective.
Article Summary: ILT20 Season 5 – Desert Vipers to begin title defence on November 21 against MI Emirates. ILT20 Interim COO Michael Fordham believes the league has established itself among the leading T20 competitions in the world. Fordham discusses the challenges of organising the new season amid uncertainty in the Middle East.

Article Title: Shubman Gill on India's WTC final hopes: 'If we win these two Tests, we will have a very good chance'
Article Text:
Shubman Gill (AFP Photo)

'Test series was our biggest priority'

Seven Tests left for India in WTC cycle

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India eye clean sweep against New Zealand

India's Test squad:

India captain Shubman Gill believes victories in both Tests against New Zealand will put the team in a strong position to qualify for the 2027 World Test Championship (WTC) final.The two-match series, which begins on November 19 in Wellington, is a major priority for India.Gill said the team had planned its preparations keeping these Tests in mind and released several players from the ODI squad to give them enough time to prepare for the red-ball format."I believe that if we win these two Test matches, we will have a very good chance of reaching the World Test Championship final. That was our focus even before arriving here. I knew these two matches would be crucial to our chances of qualifying for next year's final, which is why we pulled most of our players out of the ODI squad to ensure they had the best possible preparation and give ourselves the best chance of winning both games," Gill said ahead of the first Test.Gill also highlighted the importance of Test cricket, saying the series against New Zealand was his biggest priority among the three formats."In terms of priorities, if you had asked me a month ago which of the three series I would most want to win, it would definitely have been the Test series," he added.India rested pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah from the white-ball matches to prepare him for the Test series.Gill and KL Rahul were also released from the ODI squad before the final two matches to focus on their red-ball preparations.Gill missed the final two ODIs against New Zealand after being released from the squad last week.India have seven Tests remaining in the current WTC cycle. They will first play two Tests against New Zealand away from home before hosting Australia for a five-Test series as part of the Border-Gavaskar Trophy.Winning all seven matches would take India's points percentage (PCT) to around 70.37 per cent, putting them in a very strong position to qualify for the WTC final. The summit clash is scheduled to be played at The Oval from June 9 to 13, 2027.If India win six of their remaining seven Tests, their PCT could be around 64 to 66 per cent. This would keep them in contention, but their qualification could also depend on the results of Australia, South Africa and New Zealand.However, winning five or fewer Tests could put India's qualification hopes in danger. They would then need favourable results in other teams' matches to remain in the race for a top-two finish.India have already won the T20I and ODI series against New Zealand and will now look to complete a clean sweep by winning the two-Test series.The first Test will be played at the Basin Reserve in Wellington from November 19, while the second match will take place at Hagley Oval in Christchurch from November 27.Shubman Gill (C), Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul (VC), Devdutt Padikkal, Rishabh Pant (WK), Dhruv Jurel (WK), Ravindra Jadeja, Anshul Kamboj, Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep, Sai Sudharsan, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar, Mohammed Siraj and Gurnoor Brar.
Article Summary: India captain Shubman Gill believes victories in both Tests against New Zealand will put the team in a strong position to qualify for the 2027 World Test Championship (WTC) final. The two-match series, which begins on November 19 in Wellington, is a major priority for India. India have already won the T20I and ODI series and will now look to complete a clean sweep.

Article Title: 'Part of my body': Sachin Tendulkar gifts 25 bats to MCA Museum
Article Text:
Former Indian cricketer Sachin Tendulkar poses for photographs during the unveiling of the 'Batography' exhibition at the MCA Sharad Pawar Cricket Museum at Wankhede Stadium, in Mumbai. (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: He made them wait for a year, but when cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar finally handed over some of his memorabilia to the Mumbai Cricket Association’s (MCA) Sharad Pawar Cricket Museum, it turned out to be worth the wait.On Monday, Tendulkar, in the presence of his entire family, donated 25 of his possessions to the MCA’s Cricket Museum. These included the first bat he received from his elder sister Savita when he was five years old. She had got the bat for him from Kashmir.Explaining what his bats meant to him, Tendulkar said, "It's an extension of my body. So, I'm giving you a part of my body. Please take care of it.”In return, the MCA gifted Tendulkar a piece of turf from the Wankhede Stadium outfield.The MCA had approached Tendulkar for his memorabilia last year. However, his son Arjun was getting married at the time, and his house was also undergoing renovation. Recalling the delay, Tendulkar said, "At that time, there was a wedding at home. So, a lot of preparations were going on. And coincidentally, at that time we were also renovating our place. So, we had to move out of our house for two years, and then come back to my house.But in the meantime, I had told the (MCA) president (Ajinkya Naik) to 'give me some time, and I promise you I'll give you something nice'. I don't know if I've met your expectations, because Mumbai cricket has given me the foundation; I think it's just beyond words. Because everyone who plays cricket needs a platform. They need a system."Tendulkar also spoke about a phase in the mid-1990s when he played with a blank bat. During the 1996 World Cup, where he finished as the tournament's leading run-scorer with 523 runs in seven matches at an average of 87.16, including two centuries and three half-centuries, he used a bat without a sponsor's sticker.Explaining why he chose not to promote certain brands, Tendulkar recalled, "The reason was simple. At home, my whole family had decided that I will never promote alcohol and tobacco. And that was a period where tobacco and alcohol companies were putting their stickers on the bat. So I said that I'll wait for some manufacturing company, or whoever, other than these two brands. And I ended up, for close to two years, being without any sticker on the bat. ”Tendulkar revealed that a major foreign brand had approached him during the 1996 World Cup, but he was reluctant to change his bat's appearance while he was in good form. He recalled being named Player of the Match in the first two games and said he wanted to continue using the blank bat for the rest of the tournament."During the World Cup, in the first two matches, I was named as the 'Man of the Match.' I was feeling good with a blank bat. In those days, if you knew an individual from the dressing room, guys would actually walk in there.We were playing at (the) Wankhede (Stadium) against Australia. We were batting second. I still remember- I wouldn't name a brand- but it was a foreign brand. The MD of that company comes to the dressing room. And he said, ‘We accept all your terms and conditions. You please put the sticker on the bat and go out to bat. But I said, 'No. I'm slightly superstitious now. With the blank bat, it was priceless to score those runs.’ So I said, 'We'll talk after the World Cup is over.' Right now, the whole World Cup, I'm going to play with a blank bat.’ And that wasn't a tobacco bag or alcohol brand. It was a proper international sports brand. I was superstitious. Sometimes, it gets stuck in my head,” the cricket legend recalled.Tendulkar also spoke about why he never threw his bat on the ground, even when he was upset or angry. He said the values instilled by his father taught him to respect his cricketing equipment and the talent he had been given."I still remember that my father used to say, that keeping your things in your pocket, that includes your talent. It's a God's gift. So, you have to keep it in your pocket and worship it. My upbringing was like that. I don't think that throwing bats is a big deal. My question is, why should you throw bats? What are you going to achieve? Why don't you respect your gift? If someone asks me, if someone says something like that, I don't like it. I respect that it's not a big deal. But I have to respect it."
Article Summary: Sachin Tendulkar donated 25 of his possessions to the MCA’s Cricket Museum. These included the first bat he received from his elder sister Savita when he was five years old. The MCA gifted Tendulkars a piece of turf from the Wankhede Stadium outfield.

Article Title: 'Selector jahan baitha hai, wahin maarna hai': MS Dhoni movie inspires Suryakumar Yadav's India comeback bid
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: India T20I batter Suryakumar Yadav is determined to return to the national team and is making his presence felt in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy 2026.The Mumbai captain has scored two consecutive half-centuries in the tournament, showing signs of a return to form. After losing his place in the Indian T20I team earlier this year, Suryakumar is looking to catch the attention of the BCCI selectors with consistent performances.He scored an unbeaten 60 off just 21 balls against Hyderabad in Mumbai's tournament opener on November 14. He followed it up with an even bigger knock against Gujarat on Monday, smashing 82 off 29 balls.After his explosive innings against Hyderabad, Suryakumar spoke about his approach and revealed that his focus was on scoring runs consistently and helping Mumbai win matches.He also recalled a famous dialogue from the film 'M.S. Dhoni: The Untold Story' while explaining his mindset."You must have watched the movie 'M.S. Dhoni: The Untold Story' where Mahi bhai's friend had said, 'Selector jahan baitha hai, wahin maarna.' My plan was also the same today. I'm trying to score runs as consistently as possible, help win matches, and play the 'high-risk, high-reward' game at Nos. 3 to 5," Suryakumar told reporters.Shiv Sundar Das, a member of the BCCI Senior Men's Selection Committee representing the East Zone, was also present at the ground.A few IPL scouts were also watching the match as Suryakumar attacked the Hyderabad bowlers.One of his sixes even went beyond the Jadavpur University 2nd Ground in Salt Lake.Suryakumar made it clear that he was not trying to send any special message to the selectors. He simply wanted to enjoy his batting and play the way he always had."It's not about making any statement or anything; I just want to enjoy the way I've always played. Entertainment wala format hai, khul ke khelo ekdum," stated Suryakumar.He also spoke about the six he enjoyed hitting straight down the ground and explained how his practice was helping him execute such shots in matches."I enjoyed watching the six I hit straight down the ground. But I have been practising it a lot. And if you execute on the ground what you've done in practice, that means your practice is successful," he added.Suryakumar continued his impressive run on Monday, smashing 82 off 29 balls against Gujarat in Mumbai's Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy match.Mumbai chased down Gujarat's target of 198 in just 15.4 overs. Suryakumar's innings included seven sixes and nine fours, while Sarfaraz Khan provided support with an unbeaten 40 off 17 balls.Gujarat had posted 197, thanks to late contributions from Ashutosh Sharma (42 off 22 balls) and Vishal Jayswal (38 off 21 balls).Shardul Thakur and Atharva Ankolekar picked up three wickets each for Mumbai.Suryakumar had earlier scored an unbeaten 60 off 21 balls against Hyderabad on November 14. The two consecutive half-centuries have given him a strong start to his campaign as he looks to fight his way back into the Indian team.
Article Summary: Mumbai captain Suryakumar Yadav has scored two consecutive half-centuries in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy 2026. He scored an unbeaten 60 against Hyderabad in Mumbai's tournament opener on November 14. He followed it up with an even bigger knock against Gujarat on Monday, smashing 82 off 29 balls.

Article Title: 'Must be taught how to behave': Vengsarkar criticises India players' conduct against Pakistan after U19 Asia Cup win
