MUMBAI: Former India captain and chief selector Dilip Vengsarkar has criticised the conduct of players following India's victory over Pakistan in the Under-19 Asia Cup final on Saturday, saying such celebrations send the wrong message to young cricketers and undermine the spirit of the game.The scenes that followed India's dramatic triumph sparked intense debate even among the sane and reasonable cricket fans in India after Indian players rushed onto the field and celebrated wildly, with emotions spilling over at the end of the fiercely contested clash. One player got very close to Pakistan's wicket-keeper and screamed obscenities in his face. A few others directed profanities at the Pakistan dressing room and players with indecent gestures.Vengsarkar, who was part of many feisty India-Pakistan battles himself, however, felt there could be no justification for such behaviour, regardless of the occasion. "This is not good for the game at all. Youngsters watch these things on television and then try to emulate them when they play Under-14, Under-16 or Under-19 cricket. Where are we going if this continues? Players must be taught how to behave on and off the field, whether through the National Cricket Academy (COE) or other channels," he told TOI.The former batting great acknowledged the intense emotions associated with India-Pakistan contests. "I understand that India-Pakistan matches are highly emotional and passions run high. But that does not mean you behave in a manner that is unacceptable. Such behaviour creates the wrong impression on youngsters," he said, urging players to maintain decorum.Vengsarkar, who is actively involved in promoting grassroots cricket in Mumbai, revealed that he has increasingly noticed similar behaviour at the junior level. "I see the same thing at my academies. Whenever teams win, players run onto the ground, remove the stumps and start dancing. This never happened before. They watch these scenes on television and then copy them," he said.Demanding stronger intervention from cricket's governing authorities, Vengsarkar says the ICC, Asian Cricket Council and match officials must send a clear message on acceptable conduct. "There has to be some sort of code of conduct.A stronger message must come from the ICC, the ACC and from match referees," he said.The 70-year-old also suggested that players should be formally briefed before tournaments begin. "Before every tournament, officials should address the players, whether they are Under-19, Under-17 or Under-23 cricketers, and clearly explain what is acceptable behaviour and what is not," he said.While acknowledging that match officials may find it difficult to control spontaneous celebrations after a last-ball finish, Vengsarkar said coaches too must play a proactive role. "I saw Bangladesh do something similar a couple of years ago (2020 U-19 WC final), Pakistan did it during this tournament and now India has done it. There cannot be any justification. Nobody should be doing it," he said."The important thing is to set the right example. Young cricketers are always watching and learning from what they see at the highest level."
Article Summary: Dilip Vengsarkar criticises conduct of players following India's victory over Pakistan in the Under-19 Asia Cup final on Saturday. Former India captain and chief selector says such celebrations send the wrong message to young cricketers and undermine the spirit of the game.

Article Title: Best ever! From 14 medals to 114: How India achieved more with fewer athletes at the Asian Para Games
Article Text:
Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

From 14 medals to 114: India's remarkable rise

India's Asian Para Games record

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Smaller contingent, bigger return

Hangzhou vs Aichi-Nagoya

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Athletics powers India's medal surge

India's leading medal-winning sports in Asian Para Games 2026

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Multiple medallists underline India's depth

Paralympic progress provides the wider context

Fourth place sets a new benchmark

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

From 14 medals in 2010 to 114 in 2026, India’s remarkable rise continued in Aichi-Nagoya as a smaller contingent surpassed its previous best, achieved 30 gold medals and secured its highest-ever finish at the continental para-sport showpiece.India’s campaign at the Asian Para Games 2026 was a triumph that few would have predicted when the size of the contingent became known. With just 167 athletes travelling to Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, the prospect of repeating the 100-plus medal haul achieved at Hangzhou in 2023 appeared ambitious. The previous edition had seen India send more than 300 athletes to the competition, returning with a record 108 medals after subsequent revisions to the original tally.But the Indian contingent defied expectations, producing an even bigger return with significantly fewer athletes. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place, both the highest medal tally and the best finish in the country's history at the event.The numbers tell a compelling story of progress. India improved its medal tally for the fifth consecutive edition, added to its gold-medal record and finished ahead of South Korea, which had threatened to challenge its position in the final standings.More than the record itself, the achievement highlighted how far India's para-sport movement has travelled in 16 years — from a modest 14-medal return at the inaugural edition in 2010 to a fourth-place finish among Asia's leading para-sport nations.India's progress at the Asian Para Games has been steady, with each edition bringing a new high in the overall medal tally.At Guangzhou in 2010, India won 14 medals — one gold, four silver and nine bronze — to finish 15th. The 2014 edition in Incheon brought a substantial improvement, with the country collecting 33 medals, including three gold, but remaining 15th in the standings.The breakthrough arrived at Jakarta in 2018. India's medal tally rose to 72, comprising 15 gold, 24 silver and 33 bronze, while its position improved to ninth.Hangzhou in 2023 marked another major leap. India crossed the 100-medal barrier for the first time, initially returning with 111 medals before the tally was revised to 108 following a doping-related disqualification and a medal reallocation. The revised haul comprised 27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze, with India eventually classified sixth.Aichi-Nagoya extended that upward trajectory. India added six medals to its revised Hangzhou total, increased its gold-medal count from 27 to 30 and climbed two places to fourth.The numbers at a glance: India's medal tally increased more than eightfold between 2010 and 2026. Its gold-medal count grew from one to 30, while its position improved from 15th to fourth.The rise has not been limited to the overall tally. India has improved its standing in three successive editions since 2014, moving from 15th to ninth, then sixth and now fourth. The 2026 result represents the culmination of a sustained upward trend rather than an isolated breakthrough.The most striking feature of India's latest performance was the efficiency with which its athletes converted participation into medals.India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi-Nagoya. That was considerably fewer than the 309 athletes listed for the Hangzhou campaign in 2023, yet the team surpassed its previous best by six medals.The comparison is revealing. India sent approximately 46 per cent fewer athletes than it did to Hangzhou, but its medal tally increased by nearly six per cent. The gold-medal count rose by three, the silver tally by three, and the bronze count remained unchanged.On a simple medals-per-athlete measure, India's return increased from approximately 0.35 medals per athlete in Hangzhou to 0.68 in Aichi-Nagoya. This is an aggregate comparison, not an individual success rate, since athletes can win multiple medals and the number of events and opportunities varies across sports.Nevertheless, the figures underline the scale of the achievement. A smaller squad did not merely match the previous edition's success; it established a new benchmark for Indian para-sport.Para-athletics was the backbone of India's campaign, delivering 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. That represented nearly 57 per cent of the country's overall tally and made athletics the single biggest contributor to India's fourth-place finish.Para-badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze. Together, athletics and badminton accounted for 81 medals, more than 70 per cent of India's total.Swimming contributed 11 medals, comprising three silver and eight bronze. Archery added six medals, including three gold and three silver, while shooting produced five, with two gold, two silver and one bronze.Athletics' contribution also illustrates how India's progress has accelerated. At Hangzhou, para-athletics produced 52 medals, including 16 gold, 17 silver and 19 bronze. In Aichi-Nagoya, the discipline's haul rose to 65, with six additional gold medals.Badminton's contribution was different. India won 21 medals in the sport at Hangzhou, including four gold, but finished with 16 in 2026. Instead, the substantial gains in athletics and the contributions from other sports helped compensate for the decline in badminton medals.That distinction matters: the record haul reflects both the strength of India's established medal-winning disciplines and the need to broaden its success across events in future editions.India's record was supported by athletes who delivered more than once during the competition. A total of 26 Indian athletes won multiple medals, while six athletes collected multiple gold medals, demonstrating the importance of individual excellence in a campaign involving 11 sports.Archer Sheetal Devi was among the standout performers, winning two gold medals and a silver. Her two golds came in the mixed compound and individual compound events, while the silver added to her three-medal haul.Athletics provided several other multiple gold medallists. Dilip Gavit, Nishad Kumar, Pranav Soorma and Simran Sharma each won two gold medals, while shooting contributed through Mona Agarwal, who also secured two golds.Four athletes finished with three medals apiece: Sheetal Devi in archery, Thulasimathi Murugesan in badminton, Ravi Budigina in swimming and Himanshu Nandal in swimming. Their performances illustrated how athletes winning across multiple events can make a significant difference to a country's final tally.The figures also invite comparison with Hangzhou, where 25 Indian athletes won multiple medals. The increase to 26 in 2026 was modest, but the overall tally improved despite a much smaller contingent. The result points to a campaign in which medal-winning performances were concentrated among a relatively small squad.India's rise at the Asian Para Games has coincided with a significant improvement at the Paralympics, strengthening the country's standing in international para-sport.At Rio 2016, India won four medals and finished 43rd. Tokyo 2020 marked a breakthrough, with 19 medals — five gold, eight silver and six bronze — lifting India to 24th. At Paris 2024, India recorded its best Paralympic haul of 29 medals, comprising seven gold, nine silver and 13 bronze, to finish 18th.The progression at the Paralympics mirrors the broader trend at the Asian Para Games: larger medal returns, more gold medals and improvements in the standings.India's able-bodied contingent had also finished fourth at the 2026 Asian Games, although its 85-medal tally was below the 106 medals achieved at Hangzhou in 2023. The para contingent's performance offered a contrasting story of growth, with its medal count rising and its position improving.China dominated Aichi-Nagoya, finishing with 435 medals, including 207 gold. Hosts Japan were second with 186 medals, while Uzbekistan finished third with 145. India placed fourth with 114, ahead of South Korea, which collected 100 medals, including 29 gold.India's final position was not guaranteed until the closing stages. South Korea remained within reach, but its final-day return of one gold and two silver left it one gold behind India. The Indian contingent held on to fourth place with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze.The gap to third-placed Uzbekistan shows that further progress will require India to expand its medal-winning strength across disciplines. Yet the immediate achievement is significant: India has moved from 15th at the first two editions to fourth, while increasing its tally at every successive Games.The challenge now is to sustain that momentum, build a deeper pool of competitive athletes and reduce dependence on a handful of disciplines.For a contingent of just 167 athletes, 114 medals represent more than a record. They mark the latest step in a 16-year transformation of Indian para-sport — one that began with 14 medals in Guangzhou and has now culminated in a historic fourth-place finish in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi- Nagoya. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place. It is the best finish in the country's history at the event.

Article Text:

India returned from the Asian Para Games in Nagoya with its best-ever medal haul of 114 medals, powered by world records, golden doubles and medal-winning debuts. MONA AGARWAL : A golden double and a world recordMona Agarwal won the women’s 10m air rifle standing SH1 gold before setting a world record in the 50m rifle three positions SH1. Her score of 357.5 secured a second title and made her the first Indian para-shooter to medal in the event. The Jaipur-based Paris Paralympics bronze medallist trained for the 50m event with a rented rifle, travelling long distances to train. PRANAV SOORMA : Two titles, two recordsPranav Soorma claimed the men’s discus throw F51/52/53 gold with an Asian-record effort of 11.66m, then added the club throw F51 title with a Games-record 32.87m. Paralysed after a spinal cord injury at 16, Soorma rebuilt his life through education and sport. His Nagoya double followed club throw gold at the previous Asian Para Games and silver at the Paris Paralympics. NISHAD KUMAR : Two disciplines, two gold medalsNishad Kumar ventured beyond his high jump speciality to win the men’s T47 long jump with an effort of 7.11m, then claimed high jump gold with a Games-record clearance of 2.04m.The double Paralympic silver medallist took on the additional discipline despite a troublesome knee, showcasing his versatility.SIMRAN SHARMA: Silver to goldSimran Sharma won the women’s 200m and 100m T12 titles, improving on her two silvers at the previous Games. The visually impaired sprinter from Ghaziabad followed her 200m triumph with a Games-record 12.02s in the 100m, finishing ahead of Iran’s Hajar Safarzadeh.SHEETAL DEVI: Golden comebackSheetal beat Singapore’s Nur Syahidah Alim in the women’s individual compound final. Article Title: Asian Para Games bronze leaves Suhas Yathiraj hungry for gold amid IAS duties and badminton
Article Text:

Third Paralympics, one big dream: Gold at LA 2028

IAS officer by day, shuttler by night

NEW DELHI: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. Having beaten Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan in their group match just days earlier, the Indian shuttler had hoped to reach the final and fight for gold.Suhas lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23-21, 8-21, 15-21. He had chances to take the opening game but failed to convert them. After bouncing back to win the second game 21-8, he lost focus at a crucial stage of the decider.“Definitely not satisfied with bronze. I think if I had played up to my full potential, I would have definitely done better. In fact, I defeated Fredy of Indonesia in the group match in Nagoya only a few days ago,” Suhas told TimesofIndia.com from Aichi-Nagoya in Japan.“In the semifinal match, the first set was very close. I lost 23-21 and I had game point, set point, but I couldn't convert that. In the second set, I won very easily. In the third set, I think after 10-all, I sort of lost focus for two to three rallies. That is where he took the game. So, it was not my best day, I would assume. I would always love to win a gold medal. So, yes, I am a little sad from that angle,” he said.The defeat also reminded him of how important it is to perform under pressure at major tournaments.“It is the most important factor to win medals at major games because you might be training well, you might actually have the fitness and the skills. But if you don't recreate that during the major games, then probably it is of not much use in terms of professional success,” Suhas said.Suhas, an IAS officer, said he had never imagined representing India in international badminton a decade ago.In November 2016, he made his debut at the Asian Championships in Beijing and won gold. Since then, he has won several medals at major international events. These include bronze at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, silver at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, another silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, gold at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games and bronze in Nagoya.The 43-year-old has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024, winning silver on both occasions.With the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics approaching, the big question is whether he can go one step further and win gold.The desire is there, but Suhas is not looking too far ahead. He wants to take things one step at a time.“If you had asked me 10 years ago, I didn't even know that I would play for India. But whenever I look at the medals and the love I have got from fans and sportspersons around the world, the journey has been quite satisfying. I have had the honour of wearing the Indian jersey and winning medals for my country,” he said.“I am grateful for what God has given me. I never imagined that I would become an IAS officer one day, an Arjuna awardee or a badminton player winning medals for India. I never imagined all this. But thanks to the Almighty for all these,” Suhas, who is also an Arjuna Award recipient, said.“So if God and destiny have been kind to me, I hope they will take me to a place that I deserve. I hope I can do the best that I can in whatever I choose to,” he added.For most people, the end of a hectic working day is a time to relax, spend time with family, play with their children or watch a movie.For Suhas, it is often time to pick up his badminton racket and head to the court. His day includes early-morning gym sessions, office work, inspections, meetings, video conferences and checking files. Despite his demanding responsibilities as an IAS officer, he makes time for badminton and follows a strict fitness routine to compete at the highest level.Balancing the two careers is not easy, but his love for the sport keeps him going.“If you choose what you love, then the journey becomes painless. You enjoy that journey. That's what I do,” Suhas said.Explaining how he manages his work and training, he said: “It is challenging. My training generally starts in the night and it always involves sacrifices. Probably others would be spending time with their family members or having leisure time. My leisure time is to play badminton. In badminton, you need an extremely high level of fitness. It's challenging, hectic but at the same time I love it.”“I don't remember eating sweets in the last many months. I can't recall when I had my last sweet. So, I almost don't eat sweets or fried food and am also quite conscious about the nutrition that I take,” he said.Suhas grew up watching Malaysian badminton great Lee Chong Wei and was inspired by his movement on the court.“Yes, I have always been inspired by so many top players in the able-bodied category. Growing up, I watched the matches of Lee Chong Wei and how he used to move around the court,” he said.“Even in India, the top shuttlers perform extremely well, whether it is Lakshya Sen, HS Prannoy or Kidambi Srikanth. I know them personally and have always admired how well they are able to compete at the top,” Suhas signed off.
Article Summary: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. The Indian shuttler lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23- 21, 8-21, 15-21. Suhas has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024.

Article Title: Asian Para Games conclude in Nagoya: India sign off with record 114 medals, finish fourth
Article Text:
India finish fourth as China lead medal standings at Asian Para Games.

NEW DELHI: India signed off from the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games with their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals as the week-long continental competition concluded with a closing ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletics Stadium in Nagoya, Japan, on Saturday.Double gold medallists Nishad Kumar and Mona Agarwal led the Indian contingent as flag-bearers at the ceremony, marking the end of a landmark campaign in which the country's para-athletes delivered historic victories, world-record performances and podium sweeps across disciplines.India finished fourth in the overall standings with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, surpassing its previous best of 108 medals at the 2022 Hangzhou Games.Held in Japan for the first time, the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games brought together around 4,000 athletes and staff from 45 countries and regions. The competition featured 18 sports, with more than 20 world records reportedly set during the seven-day event.China topped the medal table with 435 medals, including 207 gold, while hosts Japan finished second with 186 medals — 64 gold, 60 silver and 62 bronze.Uzbekistan emerged as the third-ranked nation, collecting 145 medals, including 45 gold.India's fourth-place finish was particularly significant given the size of its contingent. A total of 168 para-athletes represented the country at Aichi-Nagoya, compared with 309 at the previous edition in Hangzhou.President Droupadi Murmu congratulated the Indian contingent on its record performance, saying the achievement reflected the athletes' hard work, perseverance and self-belief.In a post on X, Murmu said the unprecedented medal haul would inspire young people to dream big, work with dedication and remain positive in the face of challenges. She also extended her congratulations to the entire Indian contingent.Para athletics was India's biggest medal contributor, accounting for 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. Para badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze.India also won 11 medals in para swimming, seven in para table tennis, six in para archery and five in para shooting. The contingent added two medals each in para judo and para powerlifting.The closing ceremony brought together athletes, officials and dignitaries to mark the conclusion of the Games. Asian Paralympic Committee president Majid Rashed declared the event closed, highlighting the growing strength of para sport across Asia and its role in building a more inclusive society.Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi also praised the athletes' determination, teamwork and sportsmanship, describing their performances as a reminder of the “profound beauty” of para sports.The Asian Para Games began in Guangzhou, China, in 2010, evolving from the Far East and South Pacific Games Federation for the Disabled. The Aichi-Nagoya edition was the fifth staging of the event, with Doha, Qatar, scheduled to host the sixth in 2030.For India, the closing ceremony marked the end of a historic campaign — one that raised the country's medal benchmark and showcased the depth and growing strength of its para-sport movement.
Article Summary: India finished fourth in the overall standings with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, surpassing its previous best of 108 medals at the 2022 Hangzhou Games. A total of 168 para-athletes represented the country at Aichi-Nagoya, compared with 309 at the previous edition in Hangzhou.

NEW DELHI: India signed off from the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya with a historic performance, securing their best-ever finish of fourth place and their biggest medal haul across the five editions of the continental event.With the competition concluding on Saturday and only the Closing Ceremony remaining, India finished with a record 114 medals, including 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze. The fourth-place finish also marked a new high for the Indian contingent at the Asian Para Games, underlining the progress made by the country’s para-athletes on the continental stage.India had entered the final day in fourth place, but their position was not confirmed as South Korea remained within striking distance. The Korean contingent needed two more gold medals to draw level with India’s tally of 30, with their superior silver count potentially pushing them ahead.South Korea added three medals on the final day, taking their overall tally to 100. However, they won only one gold, along with two silver medals, and finished fifth with 29 gold, 38 silver and 33 bronze.That left South Korea one gold short of India, ensuring the Indian contingent retained fourth place.Iran, who finished sixth with 26 gold medals, were also unable to mount a late challenge to India’s position.India’s final tally of 114 medals surpassed their previous best of 108 at the 2022 Asian Para Games in Hangzhou. The 30 gold medals also set a new benchmark for the country at the event.The performance was built on strong contributions across disciplines, with athletics, badminton, archery and shooting among the key medal-winning sports. India’s athletes produced several standout performances and record-breaking efforts during the week-long competition.China topped the standings by a substantial margin, finishing with 217 gold medals and 435 medals overall. Hosts Japan placed second with 186 medals, including 64 gold, while Uzbekistan took third with 145 medals, including 45 gold.India followed in fourth with 114 medals, ahead of South Korea, Iran, Thailand, Indonesia, Kazakhstan and Saudi Arabia in the top 10.Thailand finished seventh with 125 medals overall, despite having fewer gold medals than the nations above them. Indonesia were eighth, followed by Kazakhstan in ninth and Saudi Arabia in 10th.India’s campaign in Aichi-Nagoya will be remembered for its record medal haul and best-ever finish. The fourth-place result, achieved despite a smaller contingent than the one sent to Hangzhou in 2022, gives the country a new benchmark to build on at the next edition of the Asian Para Games.The final top 10 medal standings reflect China’s dominance and the strong performances of Japan and Uzbekistan, while India’s fourth-place finish represents a historic milestone for the country’s para-sport movement.
Article Summary: India finish in fourth place at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya. Record medal haul of 114, including 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze. China topped the standings with 217 gold medals and 435 medals overall. Hosts Japan placed second with 186 medals, including 64 gold, while Uzbekistan took third with 145 medals.

NEW DELHI: India's para-athletes produced a spectacular finish to their campaign at the Asian Para Games, registering their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals, including 30 gold, after a record-breaking final-day flourish in Aichi-Nagoya on Friday.India collected nine gold medals on the day — their biggest single-day haul of the ongoing edition — with champions emerging from badminton, archery, shooting and athletics. The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023.The achievement was particularly significant as India competed with a contingent of 168 athletes, nearly half the size of the squad that represented the country in Hangzhou.India remained fourth in the standings at the end of its campaign, although the final positions could change after a few remaining events on Saturday.Athletics remained India's biggest medal contributor, accounting for 65 medals, 12 more than at the previous edition. On Friday, however, the spotlight was shared with a superb badminton campaign and gold-winning performances in shooting and archery. Star javelin thrower Sumit Antil led an Indian 1-2-3 finish in the men's F42-44/61-64 combined event . The reigning Paralympic and world champion threw 72.46m to defend his title, while Mahendra Gurjar took silver with 59.03m and Sandip Sanjay Sargar claimed bronze with 64.48m. Gurjar finished ahead of Sargar on Raza points, which determine rankings in combined-classification events.Pranav Soorma added another gold in the men's club throw F51, defending his title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m. Dharambir secured bronze with 27.71m.Sandeep delivered a world-record performance in the men's 400m T64, clocking 52.28 seconds for gold. India's Ajay Kumar also reached the podium, winning bronze in a Games-record time of 53.61 seconds.Haney produced another world record, throwing 60.49m to win the men's javelin F37/38 title. India also picked up silver medals through Nimisha Chakkungalparambil in the women's long jump T47 and Parmod Bijarnia in the men's 1500m T46, where he clocked 4:09.65.India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar and Games debutant Naveen Sivakumar.Nitesh defeated compatriot and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in the men's singles SL3 final. He later added a silver medal in mixed doubles SL3-SU5 alongside Thulasimathi Murugesan.Naveen, meanwhile, defeated Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 to win the men's singles SL4 title. Thulasimathi enjoyed a memorable campaign of her own , combining with Manasi Joshi to win gold in women's doubles SL3-SU5. The Indian pair beat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final.The 24-year-old also secured silver in women's singles SU5 after losing 18-21, 11-21 to Yang in the final, completing a three-medal haul.Shooter Mona Agarwal added another golden chapter to India's campaign, shattering the world record to win the women's 50m rifle 3 positions SH1 title with a score of 357.5 points.The 38-year-old had earlier won the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 gold with a Games-record score of 250.0 points, edging compatriot Avani Lekhara, who took silver with 249.6.Mona's latest triumph gave her a second gold of the Games and further underlined her standing among India's leading para-shooters. She had also secured India's first 2028 Paralympic quota earlier this year.In archery, Paralympic champion Harvinder Singh teamed up with debutant Vijay Sundi to win the men's recurve doubles gold, defeating China's Yun Duo and Zhao Lixue 5-1 in the final.India's women's recurve doubles pair of Bhawna Choudhary and Pooja Jatyan settled for silver after losing 0-6 to China's Gao Zihan and Wang Xueqian.India's swimmers also exceeded expectations, finishing the Games with 11 medals, including three silver. Himanshu Nandal completed a hat-trick of bronze medals by finishing third in the men's 100m freestyle S11. The 22-year-old, who was born blind due to optic nerve failure, clocked 1:05.90, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita (58.22) and China's Chuanzhen Sun (58.70).Nandal had earlier won bronze in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. Ravi Budigina also finished with three medals, comprising two silver and one bronze.With nine gold medals on Friday and a record overall haul of 114, India signed off from its Asian Para Games campaign with its most successful performance at the continental event, surpassing the benchmark set in Hangzhou three years ago.

The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023. India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar.

NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a golden double in para-athletics at the Asian Para Games on Friday, with star javelin thrower Sumit Antil leading a podium sweep and Pranav Soorma defending his title in the men's club throw F51 event.Antil successfully defended his gold in the men's javelin throw F42-44/61-64 combined event, while Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar completed an all-Indian podium finish. Soorma, meanwhile, added another gold to his collection with a Games-record performance in the club throw.The results added to India's medal haul as the country's para-athletes continued to deliver strong performances in Aichi-Nagoya.The 28-year-old Antil, a two-time Paralympic gold medallist and world record holder, produced a best throw of 72.46m in his second attempt to claim gold.Although he could not surpass his personal best, Antil was comfortably ahead of the field while competing in the F64 classification. He had won gold at the 2023 Asian Para Games with a then-world-record throw of 73.29m before improving the mark to 74.82m in May this year.Gurjar secured silver with a throw of 59.03m, while Sargar took bronze with an effort of 64.48m.Despite Sargar recording the longer distance, Gurjar finished ahead because of his superior Raza points score, which is used to determine rankings in combined events involving athletes from different classifications.The F42, F44, F62 and F64 categories are combined in certain field events, including javelin and discus throw, to create a larger and more competitive field. The classifications cover athletes with lower-limb impairments, with some competing without prostheses and others using them.Soorma continued India's gold rush by successfully defending his men's club throw F51 title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m.The Indian had won gold in the same event at the previous edition of the Asian Para Games and claimed silver at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.South Korea's Jiwon Jung took silver with a personal-best throw of 28.40m, while Dharamvir secured bronze with 27.71m to give India another double podium finish.The F51 classification is for athletes with significant movement limitations affecting the trunk, legs and hands, with varying degrees of impairment in arm movement. Who is Himanshu Nandal?

From Paris Paralympics qualification to Asian Para Games medals

NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal made his mark at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, completing a hat-trick of bronze medals with another podium finish in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday.The 22-year-old clocked 1 minute 5.90 seconds to finish third, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita, who won gold in a Games-record time of 58.22 seconds, and China's Chuanzhen Sun, who took silver in 58.70 seconds.Nandal's latest medal added to his earlier bronze finishes in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. He became one of India's standout performers in para swimming, matching compatriot Ravi Budigina's three-medal haul at the Games, which comprised two silver medals and a bronze.Born blind due to optic nerve failure, Nandal grew up in a sports-oriented family in Rohtak, Haryana. His father had played hockey at the national level, and sport became part of his life from an early age.At four, Nandal moved to Delhi and joined the National Association for the Blind, where he learnt Braille. He initially took up judo and went on to win medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021.The change opened a new chapter in his sporting journey, as he quickly progressed from domestic competitions to the international stage.Nandal achieved a significant milestone in 2024 when he became the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.A political science graduate from the University of Delhi's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, he continued to build his experience against international opposition. In 2025, he reached two finals at the World Para Swimming Championships in Singapore.At the Asian Para Games, Nandal began his medal-winning run on Tuesday, clocking 5:10.91 to secure bronze in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event. He followed it up with another third-place finish in the 100m breaststroke before completing his hat-trick in the 100m freestyle on Friday.The S11 classification is for swimmers with visual impairment, including those with very low visual acuity or no light perception.Nandal's three-medal campaign in Japan marks another milestone in his progress as an Indian para-swimmer and adds to his growing experience at major international competitions.
Article Summary: Himanshu Nandal completes hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games 2026. The 22-year-old finished third in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday. Nandal is the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.

Thulasimathi Murugesan

Thulasimathi falls short against Yang after impressive semi-final comeback

Two more gold medal opportunities await

Who is Thulasimathi Murugesan?

India's Thulasimathi Murugesan added another medal to her growing collection at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games, settling for silver in the women's singles SU5 badminton event after losing to China's Yang Qiuxia in the final on Friday. The 24-year-old, who won silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, went down 18-21, 11-21 against the Chinese shuttler at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium.However, Thulasimathi's campaign is far from over, with the Indian still in contention for two more gold medals in the mixed doubles and women's doubles events. She will look to make amends in the remaining finals as India aim to add to their medal tally.Thulasimathi, currently ranked World No. 2, could not overcome Yang in the title clash, with the Chinese player securing the gold medal in straight games. The Indian had produced a fighting performance in the semi-finals, rallying from a game down to defeat compatriot and World No. 1 Manisha Ramdass 19-21, 21-15, 21-13 and book her place in the final.The silver medal adds to Thulasimathi's impressive record in para-badminton, following her breakthrough performance at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, where she finished runner-up in the women's singles SU5 category.Thulasimathi will have two more chances to finish her campaign on a high.She has partnered Nitesh Kumar to reach the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final, where the Indian duo will face Indonesia's Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani.The Indians booked their place in the final after overcoming China's Li Mingpan and Xiao Zuxian in a hard-fought 42-minute semi-final. Nitesh and Thulasimathi prevailed 21-19, 14-21, 21-17 to secure their place in the gold medal match.Later, Thulasimathi will team up with Manasi Girishchandra Joshi in the women's doubles SL3-SU5 final. The Indian pair will face China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian, giving Thulasimathi another opportunity to challenge for gold against the Chinese shuttler who defeated her in the singles final.Born on April 11, 2002, in Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu, Thulasimathi has established herself as one of India's leading para-badminton players. Her silver medal at the Paris 2024 Paralympics marked a major milestone in her career, while her performances at the Asian Para Games have further strengthened her standing on the international stage.She trains in Hyderabad under coaches Pullela Gopichand and Irfan Sait while pursuing a degree in veterinary science at Namakkal. In recognition of her achievements in para-badminton, including her Paralympic success, she was also honoured with the Arjuna Award.
Article Summary: Thulasimathi Murugesan won silver in the women's singles SU5 event. The 24-year- old lost to China's Yang Qiuxia 18-21, 11-21 in the final. She is still in contention for two more gold medals in the mixed doubles and women's doubles events.

Article Title: Huge boost for Argentina: Scaloni confirms first-choice goalkeeper Martinez will return against Costa Rica just 3 weeks after jaw fracture
Article Text:
Emiliano Martinez is set to return for Argentina against Costa Rica, just three weeks after suffering a fractured jaw in October.

Scaloni confirms Martinez will start after jaw injury

Argentina prepare for changes as Scaloni looks beyond Messi and Di Maria

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Costa Rica friendly offers Martinez a chance to regain match fitness

Emiliano Martinez is ready to return between the posts after several weeks away following a serious jaw injury. The Argentina goalkeeper will start against Costa Rica in Cordoba on Tuesday, with Lionel Scaloni confirming that the 34-year-old has recovered sufficiently to resume playing. His return also gives Argentina an opportunity to assess their options as they begin adjusting to the absence of some of their most influential players.Martinez sustained the injury in October following a collision with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite during Chelsea's 2-0 victory. The impact left the goalkeeper with a fractured jaw, requiring surgery and a period of rehabilitation that kept him out of action for several weeks.He returned to training earlier this month and was included in Scaloni's Argentina squad despite not having played for Chelsea since the incident. The goalkeeper was also pictured working with his international team-mates while wearing a specially made protective mask.Scaloni had considered bringing Martinez back for Argentina's 2-1 defeat to Uruguay on Friday but decided against taking the risk. Instead, Geronimo Rulli started, with Juan Musso and Santiago Beltran also available as alternatives.“Emiliano is going to play in goal, he'll be there,” Scaloni told reporters ahead of Tuesday's friendly.Explaining why he had delayed the goalkeeper's return against Uruguay, the Argentina manager added: “Maybe he was fit for the previous match, but it was a risk, and since we trust Gero (Geronimo Rulli), Juan (Musso) and Santi (Santiago Beltran), we chose to look after him. An extra three days was a prudent choice.”The Costa Rica fixture will therefore mark Martinez's return to action after his recovery, although he will still need to build up his match fitness before resuming regular football at Chelsea.Martinez's return is one of several changes expected as Argentina continue to reshape their team. Scaloni confirmed that he intends to make four or five alterations to the starting line-up against Costa Rica, depending on the final training session.The manager also acknowledged the challenge of moving forward without Lionel Messi and Angel Di Maria, two players who were central to Argentina's recent success. Rather than attempting to find direct replacements, Scaloni wants younger players to develop into important figures within the squad.“We are going to make four or five changes, depending on the final training session to see what works,” he said.“Unlike the first cycle, perhaps now we have more of a foundation and can start filling the gaps left by those great players like Messi and [Angel] Di María who are no longer with us and who are irreplaceable.“We can't truly replace them because they were among the best in the world. However, we can try to fill those gaps with young players who we believe will be with us for a long time. That's the challenge we have-to reach that maximum level, though I don't know when that will be.”Argentina will face Costa Rica at the Mario Alberto Kempes Stadium in Cordoba as they look to respond to Friday's defeat against Uruguay and finish their 2026 campaign with a positive result.For Martinez, the immediate priority will be returning to competitive action without aggravating the injury. The goalkeeper's recovery has allowed him to rejoin the national team, but Tuesday's appearance will also be an important step towards regaining his rhythm before returning to Chelsea.His presence should provide some continuity for Argentina during a period of change, particularly as Scaloni experiments with the players who will be expected to take on greater responsibility in the coming months.
Article Summary: Emiliano Martinez will start for Argentina against Costa Rica on Tuesday. Goalkeeper has been out of action for several weeks with a fractured jaw. Martinez sustained the injury during Chelsea's 2-0 win over Everton in October. Manager Lionel Scaloni will make four or five changes to his team.

Article Title: 'This would definitely help': How Bellingham's underwear billboard ad in New York reflects football's growing US appeal
Article Text:
A billboard featuring Jude Bellingham in an advertisement for Calvin Klein, is seen in New York, on November 16, 2026. (Photo/Getty Images)

Jude Bellingham has added another milestone to his growing list of achievements, this time away from the football pitch. The England and Real Madrid midfielder features on a giant Calvin Klein underwear billboard in Manhattan, New York, joining a list of celebrities who have appeared on the fashion brand's famous SoHo billboard.Measuring 75 feet by 55 feet (22.9 by 16.8 metres), the billboard overlooks one of New York's busiest shopping areas and has drawn crowds of people stopping to take photographs. Bellingham is seen striking his trademark arms-stretched celebration pose, wearing only a pair of white Calvin Klein hip briefs.The billboard has been a landmark in New York's SoHo neighbourhood for 24 years. Spanning roughly five storeys in height and a quarter of a city block in width, it has featured models, actors, singers, athletes and other celebrities over the years. Bellingham's appearance puts him in the company of names such as Bad Bunny, Jeremy Allen White and Justin Bieber.His selection also reflects the growing reach of football in the United States, which co-hosted the World Cup with Mexico and Canada. Bellingham became a social media sensation during the summer tournament, attracting attention for his performances on the pitch and his appearance."We were just in the area, and then my little sister, she was like, 'I got to see the Jude Bellingham poster' -- especially after they beat Mexico in the World Cup, right?" store manager George Lozano, was quoted as saying by news agency AFP."I personally wouldn't think (most Americans) would recognize him. I think it's still growing. It's growing in terms of the US... support for football. But I think now this would definitely help, right?"Not everyone who stopped to see the billboard was familiar with Bellingham. French tourist Roxane Marin, 33, said she liked the England midfielder but that he was not her favourite player."I like him but he's not my favorite," said Marin, who helped steer England to a famous 6-4 victory over France in the third-place playoff with an inspired 98th-minute solo spectacular."I watch football, but I can't remember if I saw that match," she said, as quoted by AFP.Marin said she had come across the billboard by chance, "but I think there are people who come on purpose."
Article Summary: Jude Bellingham features on a giant Calvin Klein underwear billboard in Manhattan, New York. The England and Real Madrid midfielder joins a list of celebrities who have appeared on the fashion brand's famous SoHo billboard. Bellingham is seen striking his trademark arms-stretched celebration pose, wearing only a pair of white Calvin Klein hip briefs.

Article Title: Jude Bellingham card worth £150,000 rejected on the spot: Collector keeps ultra-rare piece with special message inscribed by star himself
Article Text:
Ben Foster was stunned after learning a collector rejected £150,000 for Jude Bellingham’s rare one-of-one autograph card bearing his Birmingham-to-Real Madrid journey inscription/ Image: Instagram

Ben Foster stunned by rejected £150,000 offer

What makes Jude Bellingham's card so rare?

Football trading cards are attracting extraordinary sums

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A £150,000 (approx.$198,000) offer would be enough to make most collectors think twice, but one owner was not prepared to part with a rare Jude Bellingham trading card at that price. The story left former Manchester United and England goalkeeper Ben Foster astonished when it came up during a discussion about the growing football memorabilia market.Foster heard about the remarkable deal while discussing his experience at the London Card Show on his podcast, the Fozcast. The former goalkeeper, who has since built a media career through his YouTube channel and podcast, has also entered the trading card market himself, having acquired a one-of-one Rio Ngumoha card.Describing the scale of the collecting scene, Foster spoke about seeing a Rio Ngumoha one-of-one booklet change hands for £14,000. The card had been pulled during a Whatnot break, and another collector offered the owner the money after seeing its Liverpool patch and unique design.But it was a story involving Bellingham that really caught his attention. Foster's co-host, Tubes, explained that a collector had been offered £150,000 for one of the Real Madrid midfielder's cards."The London Card Show was incredible. Honestly," Foster said.He went on to describe the collections on display, some reportedly worth around £250,000, before Tubes revealed the Bellingham offer."A guy walks up, he's like - '£150,000 for that card'. Liam went no.""Wow," Foster replied.Tubes clarified that £150,000 was the opening offer, but the owner was not interested in selling.The card is a 2023/24 Topps Stadium Club Chrome UEFA Champions League Marks of Excellence Black Foil autograph, one of one. Its defining feature is a handwritten inscription by Bellingham: "Brum to the Bernabéu".The message captures the midfielder's journey from Birmingham City to Real Madrid, making the card particularly meaningful to supporters who have followed his rise. Its one-of-one status also means there is no identical copy elsewhere.According to Tubes, the owner has a strong personal connection to Bellingham, Birmingham and the player's collection, which explains why he was unwilling to accept the offer. He is also a Birmingham City supporter and owns several other Bellingham cards.The card has even been photographed at St Andrew's, Birmingham City's home ground, reflecting the connection behind the inscription.The rejected offer is another example of how much collectors are prepared to pay for rare football memorabilia, particularly cards featuring established stars and emerging talents.Foster's account of the London Card Show included the £14,000 sale of the Ngumoha card, while the wider market has seen some of the most sought-after Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo cards reach seven-figure valuations. Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton has also been associated with a card valued at around £1 million.Topps and Panini have helped expand the market, with specialist collectors' events and flagship stores in cities including London and Paris drawing greater attention to the hobby.For Bellingham's owner, however, the decision appears to go beyond the potential resale value. The inscription links the card to the player's journey and Birmingham roots, and £150,000 was not enough to persuade him to let it go.
Article Summary: Jude Bellingham's one-of-one trading card was rejected for £150,000. Ben Foster heard about the deal while talking about the football memorabilia market. The former England goalkeeper also owns a Rio Ngumoha card. The card is a 2023/24 Topps Stadium Club Chrome UEFA Champions League Marks of Excellence Black Foil autograph, one of one.

Article Title: UEFA backs French football chief Philippe Diallo to challenge Gianni Infantino for FIFA presidency
Article Text:
French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo (Reuters Photo)

UEFA flags concerns over FIFA's direction

Who is Philippe Diallo?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

French Football Federation (FFF) president Philippe Diallo will challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency in March 2027 after securing the backing of UEFA , setting the stage for a contest over the leadership and governance of world football's governing body.UEFA announced on Monday that its member associations represented on the executive committee and the FIFA Council had unanimously pledged their support for Diallo to stand against Infantino, who is seeking a fourth term as FIFA president. The election is scheduled to take place in Rabat, Morocco, on March 18, 2027."At a meeting held today and chaired by UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin, the national associations represented on the UEFA Executive Committee and the FIFA Council invited Philippe Diallo, President of the French Football Federation (FFF), to stand as a candidate in the FIFA presidential election in March 2027 and unanimously pledged their full support," a UEFA statement said.Diallo has accepted the invitation, with his candidacy due to be formally ratified by the FFF Executive Committee at its meeting on Tuesday.The development comes amid growing opposition to Infantino following his aborted proposal in July to bring private investors into a new FIFA commercial entity holding rights linked to competitions, including the World Cup. The initiative triggered concerns over transparency and governance among several European associations, with the French federation among those withdrawing support for Infantino's re-election.UEFA said its member associations wanted a change in the way the global governing body operates, calling for greater unity, trust and accountability within the football community."Against the backdrop of serious concerns over the direction of FIFA, the national associations called for renewed unity and trust within the global football community," UEFA said."They also called for a FIFA that places the development of the game in every region of the world at the heart of its mission, upholds the highest standards of governance and works in close partnership with its member associations, confederations and football stakeholders."They expressed their full confidence in Philippe Diallo to provide the leadership needed to achieve this ambition."The UEFA executive committee met on Monday to settle on a candidate ahead of Wednesday's deadline for nominations. Diallo's emergence follows discussions within the European body over finding an alternative to Infantino, who is seeking another term after becoming FIFA president in 2016.The FFF had already distanced itself from the incumbent in September, withdrawing its support for his re-election. Diallo had made his position clear at the time, saying: "the trust placed in the FIFA president has been broken".He had also indicated that European associations needed to put forward an alternative capable of contesting the election."We will need to be ready by then to put forward a candidacy capable of winning the FIFA presidency," Diallo said in September.The 63-year-old has been at the helm of French football since 2023. He was initially appointed interim FFF president in January that year following the resignation of Noel Le Graet, before being elected five months later to serve until the end of 2024. He was re-elected in December 2024 for a four-year term.Diallo joined the FFF in 2021 and became its vice-president later that year.Infantino, meanwhile, is preparing to seek a fourth term when FIFA's member associations vote in March. The Swiss-Italian administrator has faced criticism over the proposed commercial entity, which was eventually abandoned following opposition from football stakeholders.Diallo is not the only figure to have expressed an intention to challenge Infantino. Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima announced his intention to run earlier in November, while former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega was the first candidate to publicly declare his plans last month.Candidates require the backing of at least five national associations to stand in the election. With UEFA now throwing its weight behind Diallo, the contest for FIFA's top post has entered a new phase.
Article Summary: French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo will challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency in March 2027. Diallo has secured the backing of UEFA, setting the stage for a contest over the leadership and governance of world football's governing body. The 63-year-old has been at the helm of French football since 2023.
